sources.title: Basic Kettlebell instruction 9 - intro to single arm swing
Kettlebell hard vs soft style single arm swing.

sourceFacts: #67 teaches an introductory thumb-down/back single-arm swing with a low arm path and controlled parking.
#67 specifies inhale down/exhale up; no numerical training program is given.
#446 distinguishes hard-style power and soft-style/double-dip endurance as separate skills.
appDecisions: Separate opt-in block, explicit single-arm familiarity and recent two-hand swing practice.
Independent owned load/cycle, 2–4 sets of 3–5 per side, 90-second rests, planning pace and load review are app defaults.
Park between sides; bilateral actuals are required, not fictional hand-change or paired component credit.
limits: No soft-style, thumb-up, overhead or outside-swing pathway.
No universal source dose, automatic load conversion, mastery or new paired gate is inferred.
Physical technique and video timing remain unverified; no timestamps are invented.

entry.purpose: Practice the introductory single-arm hip-driven swing with controlled trunk and grip, separately on each side.
setup: Review a familiar two-hand swing and the #67 demonstration before confirming the separate single-arm skill. Use a manageable familiar bell and clear space.
Turn the handle perpendicular to the body line, step back about 12–18 inches as demonstrated, and take the handle corner with the thumb down/back. Individual setup still needs technique review.
steps: Drive the shoulder away from the ear to engage the lat. Hike back and begin with small swings.
Stand with hip and leg drive, squeeze the glutes and control the rib cage. Keep the introductory arm path low, about 45 degrees, rather than lifting with the shoulder.
On the return, hinge with the forearm tracking against the inside of the thigh as demonstrated.
Track the bell forward and park gently in its starting position. Repeat on the other side; do not change hands in the air for this movement.
bracing: Inhale down and exhale up in the introductory lesson; keep the shoulder supported and trunk controlled.
The hard-style introduction and soft-style double-dip endurance swing are different skills. This app does not prescribe the latter or its breathing patterns.
mistakes: Thumb-up technique is not the introductory variation. Review the demonstrated thumb-down/back grip rather than changing it to chase more reps.
Lifting the arm too high and raising the rib cage, or swinging below the demonstrated thigh contact: stop and review the introductory positions.
Rushed parking, deteriorating grip or trunk control: stop the set and record only actual work.
Five per side means ten total; missing or unequal side counts cannot advance this independent cycle.
